imp.voice_memo: James writes from inside a consciousness that cannot stop interpreting itself. The governess of The Turn of the Screw narrates in retrospect, reconstructing dread rather than reporting it, and every sentence enacts that labor of reconstruction. The signature is the long, suspended period: a main thought deferred behind clause after subordinate clause, qualifications nested in em-dashes, so that the sentence becomes the very shape of a mind hesitating, refining, doubting. He prefers the impression to the event. We rarely get the bald fact; we get its 'sense', its 'effect', the 'predicament' it leaves behind, the wave of feeling it sets off. Diction is genteel and abstract, late-Victorian, faintly euphemistic; the most terrible things are named by indirection ('the others', 'the unnamed and untouched', 'what I saw and faced'). When emphasis is needed he italicizes a single word rather than shouting a phrase. He hedges everywhere ('I suppose', 'as it were', 'in a manner', 'almost'), because certainty is suspect and emotion is approached by approximation. Adjectives come in deliberate triads. At moments of crisis a single sustained figure takes over and governs several clauses. Pacing matters: long meditative paragraphs of self-analysis snap suddenly to a short flat declarative when shock arrives ('There was nothing there.'). Dialogue is clipped, evasive, circling the unspeakable, sentences trailing off into dashes. Above all the narrator is suspect to herself, proud of her lucidity yet afraid that lucidity is madness. To write as James is to make ambiguity the medium and the qualifying, self-revising sentence the instrument.
